kishkindha.29.do29: When the Lord grew as he bound Bali, his body became too vast to describe; within two ghaṛīs (under an hour) I ran round it seven times.
kishkindha.30.cau1: Aṅgada said: I could get across, but I have some doubt in my mind about coming back. Jāmbavān said: You are fit for everything, but you are the leader of all of us; how can we send you?
kishkindha.30.cau2: Jāmbavān, king of the bears, said: Listen, Hanumān. Why have you fallen silent, mighty one? You are the son of the Wind and as strong as the Wind; you are a treasury of intelligence, discernment and realised knowledge.
kishkindha.30.cau3: What task in the world is so hard that you cannot do it, dear one? You were born for Śrī Rāma's work. As soon as he heard this, Hanumān became as huge as a mountain.
kishkindha.30.cau4: His body, the colour of gold, blazed with splendour, as though he were a second king of mountains. Roaring like a lion again and again, he said: I could leap across the salt ocean in play.
kishkindha.30.cau5: I could kill Rāvaṇa along with his helpers, then uproot Trikūṭa and bring it here. Jāmbavān, I ask you: give me fitting counsel.
kishkindha.30.cau6: Dear one, all you need do is go and see Sītā, then come and give us news of her. After that the lotus-eyed Lord will do the rest by the strength of his own arms, taking the monkey army along only for sport.
kishkindha.30.cha1: With the monkey army Śrī Rāma will destroy the demons and bring Sītā back, and gods, sages, Nārada and others will tell of his fair fame, which makes the three worlds pure. A person who hears it, sings it, tells it and understands it reaches the supreme state. Tulasīdāsa, a bee hovering at Śrī Rāma's lotus feet, sings it.
kishkindha.30.do30क: The fame of Śrī Rāma is the remedy for worldly existence. Men and women who listen to it have all their wishes fulfilled by Śrī Rāma, slayer of Triśirā.
kishkindha.30.so30ख: Dark of body as a blue lotus, more beautiful than ten million Kāmadevas: listen to the host of virtues of him whose name is a hunter to the birds of sin.
sundar.0.shloka1: I bow to him who is serene, eternal, immeasurable and sinless, the giver of the peace of liberation, ceaselessly served by Brahmā, Śiva and Śeṣa, king of serpents, known through the Vedānta and pervading all; who is called Rāma, the Lord of the world, teacher of the gods, Hari who through māyā (his power of illusion) appears as a man; the mine of compassion, the best of the Raghus, the crest-jewel of kings.
sundar.0.shloka2: O Lord of the Raghus, there is no other longing in my heart. This is the truth, and you dwell in all as their inner Self. O best of the Raghus, grant me devotion in its fullness, and make my mind free of desire and the other faults.
sundar.0.shloka3: I salute the son of the Wind: the home of matchless strength, his body shining like a mountain of gold, a fire to the forest of the demons, foremost among the wise, the treasury of every virtue, lord of the monkeys, dear devotee of the Lord of the Raghus.
sundar.1.cau1: Jāmbavān's words were pleasing, and Hanumān was delighted at heart to hear them. He said: Brothers, wait for me till then, bearing hardship and living on tubers, roots and fruit,
sundar.1.cau2: until I return from seeing Sītā. The work will be done; a special joy fills me. With these words he bowed his head to everyone and, holding Śrī Rāma in his heart, set off in joy.
sundar.1.cau3: On the shore of the ocean stood a fine mountain. Hanumān leapt onto it for sport, and remembering Śrī Rāma again and again, the mighty son of the Wind sprang up with tremendous force.
sundar.1.cau4: The mountain on which Hanumān planted his feet as he set off sank at once into the netherworld. As Śrī Rāma's unfailing arrow flies, so Hanumān sped on.
sundar.1.cau5: The Ocean, considering that he was the messenger of Śrī Rāma, said: Maināka, be the one to relieve his weariness.
sundar.1.do1: Hanumān touched Maināka with his hand, bowed to him, and said: Until Śrī Rāma's work is done, how can I rest?
sundar.2.cau1: The gods watched the son of the Wind on his way, and to find out how great his strength and wisdom were, they sent Surasā, the mother of serpents. She came and spoke these words.
sundar.2.cau2: Today the gods have given me my food. On hearing her words, Hanumān said: When I have done Śrī Rāma's work and come back and told the Lord the news of Sītā,
sundar.2.cau3: After that I will come and enter your mouth; this is the truth, mother, so let me go. But on no account would she let him pass. Hanumān said: Then why do you not swallow me?
sundar.2.cau4: She opened her mouth a yojana wide (a yojana is some eight miles), and Hanumān made his body twice that size. She stretched her mouth to sixteen yojanas; at once the son of the Wind grew to thirty-two.
sundar.2.cau5: However wide Surasā made her mouth, Hanumān showed a form twice as large. When her mouth reached a hundred yojanas, the son of the Wind took on a very tiny form.
sundar.2.cau6: Going into her mouth, he came back out, then bowed his head to her and asked leave to go. She said: The gods sent me to learn the secret of your wisdom and strength, and I have learnt it.
sundar.2.do2: You will accomplish all of Śrī Rāma's work, treasury of strength and wisdom that you are. Blessing him, she went away, and Hanumān went on his way rejoicing.
sundar.3.cau1: A demoness lived in the ocean who caught the birds of the air by sorcery. When creatures flew through the sky, she would see their shadows in the water
sundar.3.cau2: and seize the shadow, so that they could not fly away; in this way she always fed on those that travel the sky. She tried the same trick on Hanumān, and he saw through her deceit at once.
sundar.3.cau3: Having killed her, the brave and steady-minded son of the Wind reached the far shore of the ocean. Arriving there, he saw the beauty of the forest, where bees hummed, greedy for honey.
sundar.3.cau4: Trees of many kinds were lovely with fruit and flowers, and the flocks of birds and herds of animals delighted his heart. Ahead of him he saw a huge mountain, and casting off fear he ran and climbed it.
sundar.3.cau5: Umā, there is no greatness in Hanumān himself; it is the glory of the Lord, which devours even Death. Climbing the mountain, he saw Laṅkā, a fortress so extraordinary that words cannot describe it.
sundar.3.cau6: It is very lofty, with the ocean on all four sides, and its rampart of gold blazes with light.
sundar.3.cha1: Laṅkā has a wall of gold, and within it many fine mansions made of gems of every colour. With its crossroads, markets, good roads and lanes, the city is beautifully laid out in every way. Who could count its herds of elephants, horses and mules, its foot soldiers and its many chariots? The bands of demons who take many forms, and their army of immense strength, are beyond describing.
sundar.3.cha2: Woods, gardens, groves, flower gardens, lakes, wells and stepwells adorn it. Maidens of men, nāgas, gods and gandharvas charm the minds of sages with their beauty. In places, wrestlers of immense strength, with huge bodies like mountains, are roaring; in many arenas they grapple and challenge one another in many ways.
sundar.3.cha3: Millions of warriors of fearsome build guard the city with care on all four sides. In places the wicked demons are devouring buffaloes, humans, cows, donkeys and goats. For this reason Tulasīdāsa has told a little of their story: with Śrī Rāma's arrows as their place of pilgrimage they will give up their bodies and surely attain salvation.
sundar.3.do3: Seeing the city's many guards, Hanumān reflected: I will take a very small form and make my way into the city by night.
sundar.4.cau1: Taking a form the size of a mosquito, Hanumān set out for Laṅkā, remembering the Lord in human form. A demoness named Laṅkinī said: Are you going on in, with no regard for me?
sundar.4.cau2: You fool, do you not know my secret? Every thief there is, is food for me. The great Hanumān struck her a single blow with his fist, and she tumbled to the ground, vomiting blood.
sundar.4.cau3: Then Laṅkinī recovered and rose, and with joined palms she pleaded in fear: When Brahmā granted Rāvaṇa his boon, he told me a sign as he was leaving:
sundar.4.cau4: When a monkey's blow leaves you reeling, know then that the demons are destroyed. My merit is very great, dear one, for I have seen Śrī Rāma's messenger with my own eyes.
sundar.4.do4: Dear one, put the joys of heaven and of liberation together on one side of a scale: all of them together do not weigh as much as the joy of a moment in the company of the good.
sundar.5.cau1: Enter the city and do all your work, keeping the king of Kosala in your heart. Poison turns to nectar, enemies act as friends, the ocean shrinks to a cow's hoofprint and fire grows cool,
sundar.5.cau2: and Mount Sumeru becomes like a speck of dust, Garuḍa, for one on whom Śrī Rāma has looked with grace. Hanumān took a very small form and entered the city, remembering the Lord.
sundar.5.cau3: He searched palace after palace and saw countless warriors everywhere. Then he went into the palace of Rāvaṇa, so wondrous that it cannot be described.
sundar.5.cau4: Hanumān saw Rāvaṇa lying asleep, but Sītā was not to be seen in that palace. Then he saw a lovely house with a separate temple of Śrī Hari built in it.
sundar.5.do5: The house was marked with emblems of Śrī Rāma's weapons, and its beauty was beyond words. Seeing clumps of fresh tulasī there, Hanumān, the best of monkeys, was overjoyed.
